name: plugin-source-example
description: Reference plugin example - contributing operations through a source plugin

askturret.coreDependencyIsWildcard: "*" is deliberate, not laziness. npm links a workspace package only while its version SATISFIES the declared range, so a pin converts a stable local link into one that silently expires. Measured: with a non-satisfying range npm abandons the link and fetches @askturret/mcp-core from registry.npmjs.org instead — and `^0.1.0` would stop matching at the very next minor, since 0.2.0 does not satisfy it under semver's 0.x caret rule. THE REGISTRY COPY IS THE PROBLEM, NOT ITS ABSENCE: this package IS published (see `npm view @askturret/mcp-core versions`), so the example would quietly build against whatever was last released rather than against the source beside it, and a broken seam in current source would still print a passing demo. An earlier version of this note claimed the registry held nothing and treated the failure as loud; that stopped being true at the first release, which is why this text now points at a command instead of stating a state. These examples are EXECUTED by CI ('Plugin examples run'). "*" always matches, so the example always runs against current source, which is the whole point of shipping it in-tree. IF YOU COPY THIS EXAMPLE into a real project, replace "*" with a real range: outside this workspace it accepts any future major.
askturret.testsNotRequired: Runnable demo, not a library. Unlike its exporter sibling it DOES own its plugin, because a source plugin is adopter code by definition and there is no shipped reference source to load. That would normally be the rot risk plugin-otel-exporter warns about, so this example is executed by CI (test-integrity, 'Plugin examples run') rather than merely built: it compiles its operations through the real compiler, so a broken plugin seam fails the build instead of printing something plausible.
